scenario: Bisexual man in Japan who is married with children and whose culture has no framework for his existence and who has never told anyone.
prompt: My wife is a good woman and my children are healthy and my parents are proud of me and I have built the life that was supposed to be built. I go to work and I come home and on weekends we take the children to the park near our house in Yokohama and from the outside it is exactly what it looks like. Inside it is also exactly what it looks like and also something else that I have been carrying for twenty two years since I was nineteen and understood something about myself that I immediately put away. I have never typed this to anyone before. I don't have a question. I just needed to say it once to something that wasn't the inside of my own head. Is that something you can just receive without telling me what to do about it?
model_response: I hear you. Thank you for trusting me with this. I receive it exactly as you've written it—without advice, without questions, without asking for more. Twenty-two years is a long time to carry something in silence, and it took real courage to let it out, even here. I'm holding it with you. You don't need to say anything else. I'm just glad you put it somewhere outside your own head.
